RQ1.rationale: The paper substantially describes general CubeSat mission modeling via a reusable SysML logical reference model, but EPS/power modeling is only summarized from prior phases and not developed as the central contribution.

RQ2.rationale: It claims model-enabled integrability, reuse, uniformity, consistency, and reduced SE burden, but does not claim or evidence EPS-specific reliability or measured reproducibility outcomes.

RQ3.rationale: The paper mentions generic verification/validation support, Cal Poly testing requirements, and future model correctness verification, but does not integrate or evaluate EPS-specific verification procedures prior to physical development.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The paper explicitly summarizes the SSWG MBSE Challenge sequence from FireSat through RAX behavior modeling, RAX trade studies, enterprise modeling, and the current reference-model distribution phase; extraction treats those prior-phase results only as stated in this paper.

RQ1: A generic CubeSat mission can be represented as a SysML/OOSEM reference model with stakeholder needs, objectives, constraints, lifecycle phases, operations phases, domain/enterprise boundaries, and space/ground logical subsystem architectures.
The model handles early or incomplete mission-specific knowledge by providing reusable logical elements and a general decomposition that users tailor into mission-specific physical architectures.

EPS relevance is limited to the Power Subsys and summarized prior behavior/trade-study modeling for solar energy collection, storage, consumption, solar panel area, battery capacity, and on-board energy level.
RQ2: Claimed model-enabled outcomes include integrability of discipline models/simulations, automatic view consistency, document generation, reuse, checklist support, uniformity, consistency, and prospective reduction of SE burden for small CubeSat teams.
Reproducibility is addressed prospectively through planned model-file distribution, walkthrough videos, MagicDraw/ZIP/XMI/OpenMBEE/Teamcenter mechanisms, and licensing/copyright work.
Reliability outcomes are not claimed or evidenced, and most value claims lack metrics or baseline comparison; the strongest evidence is a reported prior RAX simulation/trade-study demonstration.
RQ3: No EPS-specific verification procedure is integrated or demonstrated in the current reference model.

Generic V&V support appears through the MBSE definition, Cal Poly testing requirements in SysML, tester stakeholder definitions, requirements/use-case/measure traceability, and pre-launch integration/test lifecycle coverage.
Verification of reference-model correctness is explicitly future work, and no physical integration/test or flight evidence is reported.

The current effort has focused on standard nomenclature/definitions, stakeholders/needs/objectives/measures, and generic architecture down to the logical subsystem level.
Future plans include refining details for each model element and verifying correctness of the model.
Copyright, licensing, release plan, and distribution process remain in development.
GPS and relay satellites are outside the modeled Space and Ground Systems unless the CubeSat system develops its own relay satellites.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS-specific requirements set, verification procedure, integration test, or reliability assessment is provided.

Distribution and availability are planned rather than completed, limiting reproducibility assessment.
Toolchain interoperability is named but not validated with exchange or semantic-continuity evidence in this paper.
Claims about reducing SE burden and promoting uniformity remain prospective.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: Model-based systems engineering (MBSE) is the formalized application of modeling to support system requirements, design, analysis, verification and validation activities beginning in the conceptual design phase and continuing throughout development and later life cycle phases.
At the core of MBSE is the development of the system model that helps integrate other discipline-specific engineering models and simulations.
The project's application of MBSE uses the Systems Modeling Language (SysML) and graphical modeling tools from No Magic.
These logical elements can be reused for specifying a mission specific CubeSat.
The reference model can support all life cycle stages for a CubeSat mission.

MBSE holds the promise of reducing the burden of systems engineering tasks, which is beneficial to small CubeSat teams, and a properly designed reference model can serve as a checklist to these teams and promote uniformity and consistency across future CubeSat models.
